QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_9

question.text: Under SEBI's operational guidelines for AIF performance benchmarking, at what frequency and on which cut-off dates must AIFs report cash-flow and valuation data to benchmarking agencies?

answer.text: Monthly, on the last business day of each calendar month.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Box 7.3 Section A (a), (e): Performance Benchmarking is done on a half-yearly basis using data as on 30-September and 31-March of each year. The 31-March data must be AUDITED; 30-September data may be UNAUDITED. **The Trap:** Monthly is for NAV internal monitoring, not benchmarking. Quarterly is for investor reporting per Reg 20. Annually is just the auditor cycle, not the benchmarking cycle. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the identical framework. XIX-A distributors rely on the half-yearly Benchmark Report for client updates. XXI-B PMS uses monthly TWR reporting — a narrower cycle than AIFs. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** As a Cat I/II Manager, align your internal valuation committee calendar with the Sep-30 and Mar-31 cut-offs PLUS the 7-month SEBI window for audited investee-company data. Running the valuation committee at odd months creates reconciliation pain.
